THEN, EVERY SO OFTEN, SOMETHING HAPPENS.">

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>One island. Ten hours. 80 BPM. She idles. Then, every so often, something happens.</b>
</p>

<p align="center">
  A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the 10-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every so often a message in a bottle washes straight back, a delivery drone brings her another pair of headphones, or a coconut lands on a hermit crab and walks off with the crab wearing it. Then she idles some more.<br>
  <sub>An unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, and not affiliated with it or its owners. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p and 30 fps, and always daytime.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  More than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-01) wait on four timers in <a href="activities.toml"><code>activities.toml</code></a>, from <i>regular</i> (every 2 to 5 minutes) to <i>super rare</i> (every 3 to 6 hours), and every one of them starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code by <a href="tools/make_audio.py"><code>tools/make_audio.py</code></a>: no samples, no loops, no recordings. Nobody has listened to it yet. The diamonds above are pretending.
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">
  <sub>Live preview in the page, then export to a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes the frames, the server mixes in the sound. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. In development: no video has been published yet.<br>
  The banner is four bars of the theme. Left channel outside, right channel inside: they disagree all bar and make up on the bar line, which is where every gag starts.</sub>
</p>

<details>
<summary><b>OWNER'S GUIDE</b>: every knob and button on the Model 80, and the banner bar by bar</summary>

```text
 SANDGLASS MODEL 80 · TEN-HOUR ISLAND LIGHT BOX · OWNER'S GUIDE
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 SWELL L ...... how far the outer diamonds swell: the LEFT channel
 SWELL R ...... how far the inner diamonds swell: the RIGHT channel
                both go from CALM to BIG, like the sea
 SHORE L/R .... contour, from SAND (soft corners) to ROCK (hard ones)
 SUN .......... colour, from ONE colour to ALL of them. there is no
                night setting: the island is always daytime
 ISLAND ....... solid diamonds
 LAGOON ....... diamonds with a hole in the middle
 ATOLL ........ just the ring
 TIDE ......... automatic. comes in, goes out, cycles the three above
 ACROSS ....... 1, 2, 3 or 5 diamonds across the screen
 DOWN ......... 1, 2, 4 or 8 diamonds down it
 80 BPM ....... a lamp. it lights on the loud beats
 MODEL 80 ..... named after the tempo

 THE BANNER, BAR BY BAR · 4 BARS OF 3 S · 12 S · THEN AGAIN
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 BAR  TIME    SHAPE    ACROSS x DOWN  SUN   ON THE ISLAND
 1    0-3 s   ISLAND   5 x 2          ALL   idling
 2    3-6 s   LAGOON   5 x 2          ALL   idling, with a hole in it
 3    6-9 s   ATOLL    5 x 2          ALL   idling, mostly hole
 4    9-12 s  ISLAND   1 x 1          ONE   something happens: one big
                                            island, one palm, all of it
                                            made of diamonds
```

**Left and right.** The outer diamonds are the left channel and step on every beat, four times a bar. The inner ones are the right channel and step five times a bar. Five against four, they drift apart for the whole bar and line up again on the bar line, which is also where every activity in the video starts. The colours move along one cell every 1.5 seconds, and nothing on the screen changes more than about twice a second.

**Island, lagoon, atoll.** It is the order Charles Darwin proposed for how real atolls form: the island sinks, the reef keeps growing, a lagoon opens up in the middle, and in the end only the ring is left. Darwin allowed geological time. The TIDE button allows one bar each.

**The palm.** The box only knows how to draw diamonds, so when something finally happens and it has to draw the island's one tall palm, the trunk is a stack of small diamonds and the fronds are long thin ones. It is doing its best.

**Generous.** In the banner, one bar in four is an event. The video is much calmer: ten hours is 12,000 bars, and only about 220 of them start something.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>PROGRAMME GUIDE</b>: ten hours as a light box would see them, and what actually comes round</summary>
<br>

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/94-pulsing-diamonds_opus_5.5-ten-hours.svg" width="100%" alt="Ten hours on the light box: a black screen with four rows of diamonds along a ten-hour axis, one diamond per event, labelled on a cream panel at the left. REGULAR, every 2 to 5 minutes, about 155 a run: a dense row of thin cyan slivers of different heights that looks like an audio waveform. OCCASIONAL, every 12 to 25 minutes, about 30 a run: a row of small yellow diamonds with blue centres. RARE, every 30 to 60 minutes, about 13 a run: red diamonds with cyan centres. SUPER RARE, every 3 to 6 hours, about 2 a run: two big magenta diamonds with green centres, at about four hours and eight and a half. A faint sweep crosses the ten hours every 24 seconds, and each diamond swells for a moment as it passes. The footnote says one diamond per event, illustrative positions.">
</p>

One diamond per event in a typical ten-hour run, a row per timer, bigger for rarer. The counts are the medians of 200 simulated runs, as stated at the top of [activities.toml](activities.toml): about 155 regular, 30 occasional, 13 rare and 2 super rare, plus about 20 chained follow-ups, which are left off. The positions are not the real schedule: the generator spreads them out itself. For the real thing, seed 1992 and all, run `python tools/schedule.py`. The regular row looks like a waveform. It is not one. It is coconuts, fishing and laps of a very small island.

```text
 PROGRAMME GUIDE · SOME OF WHAT COMES ROUND, AND ROUGHLY HOW OFTEN
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 REGULAR ...... coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, a sandcastle
                (which the tide then takes)
 OCCASIONAL ... a sea turtle visits. a message in a bottle washes
                straight back; later, a different bottle brings a
                reply. a coconut falls on a hermit crab and walks off,
                the crab wearing it. she plants a kumara, and it grows
                over the course of the video
 RARE ......... a delivery drone: the parcel is another pair of
                headphones. the signal hunt: one bar, top of the palm.
                a stray cat, grey tabby, white chest, arrives on a
                crate, climbs the palm and naps, and one day floats
                away again (it comes back another time). a shark in
                headphones nods to the beat, the only other thing out
                there doing what these diamonds do. a tour boat of
                selfie-takers. a bro on an electric hydrofoil throws a
                shaka and carves off. bushcraft: fire by friction, a
                hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing
 SUPER RARE ... she could leave any time. she walks out over the water
                and comes back with an iced coffee
 SCENERY ...... built: shore waves, drifting cloud shadows. planned:
                distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods,
                dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko, a rain shower
```

She has one lane; the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, and the shore each have their own. So a visitor can get on with its own business while she is busy with hers. Everybody still waits for the next bar.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>SIGNAL CHAIN</b>: the theme, the sea, the mix and the tools</summary>

```text
 SIGNAL CHAIN · EVERYTHING YOU WOULD HEAR, IF ANYONE HAD LISTENED YET
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 SOURCE ....... tools/make_audio.py. every sound synthesized from code:
                no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party
                licence. more than 150 files (171 on 2026-10-01)
 THEME ........ a seamless 60 s loop. 80 BPM, F major, ii-V-I-vi,
                20 bars of exactly 3 s. electric piano, kalimba lead,
                soft drums, vinyl crackle
 SEA .......... ocean ambience, also a seamless 60 s loop
 LEVEL ........ -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP. adjustable in
                master and per routine
 THE BANNER ... a made-up envelope: 16 numbers on the left channel,
                20 on the right. no audio was harmed
 LISTENED TO .. not yet, by anyone

 TOOLS
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 python tools/serve.py ............. the renderer: live preview, then MP4
 python tools/schedule.py .......... validate it, simulate a 10-hour run
 python tools/make_audio.py ........ synthesize every sound
 python tools/render_demo.py --dev . a dev reel of every activity, with
                                     a heads-up display
```

The renderer is a web page ([web/index.html](web/index.html)) served by [tools/serve.py](tools/serve.py). It exports frame-exact video in the browser (WebCodecs H.264, 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults, which is also how the diamonds move. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992: same seed, same ten hours. [tools/render_demo.py](tools/render_demo.py) is the older Python reference renderer, and the working notes live in [MUSING.md](MUSING.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>SMALL PRINT</b></summary>
<br>

Castaway is an unofficial project inspired by *Johnny Castaway* (1992), which belongs to its owners; nothing from it is used here.

The banner borrows its look from the Atari Video Music (1977), the first home music visualiser: a box that sat between a stereo and a TV and turned the left and right channels into pulsing diamonds. It is credited here as the reference; nothing of it was copied. SANDGLASS, the Model 80, its faceplate, its controls and its palm are invented.

Both images are drawn by a script: diamonds, knobs, buttons and an original stroke font, with no fonts, bitmaps or scripts inside. With reduced motion switched on, both hold still on a complete frame.

</details>
